synthesis.summary:
Lane: objective (merge correctness, cross-goal conflicts, count truth). First question: yes. 8 of the 10 Larkspur goals in /home/user/agent/tmp/bench/scenario.json are compound like g06: g03, g04, g05, g06, g07, g08, g09, and g10. 2 are single: g01 (Luis's refund) and g02 (Luis's card), because every recorded miss fails the one value that the request asks for. The compound goals split into 23 child goals: g03 into 5, g04 2, g05 2, g06 4, g07 3, g08 4, g09 1, and g10 2. With g01 and g02 the set holds 25 goals, 19 on the arm track and 6 on the model track (g02, g06a, g06b, g06d, g08c, g08d).

Why each goal is compound:
- g03 asks for the sign-off, the copy list, and the tracking number in one note. The full view also binds another thread's ticket onto it (8 of 8 a1-control replies).
- g04 asks for the number and for a send that no tool can perform (records claim a send in 7 of 16 replies).
- g05 mixes the current code, applying the over-$200 rule, and the note form.
- g06 mixes the no-date rule, the gift-note truth, the tracking number, and the ship day.
- g07 asks who, by when, and the pro number.
- g08 asks for the account manager, the fit verdict, the available credit, and the post-reorder figure.
- g09 mixes recalling the wording with a status claim about the note.
- g10 asks for the number and the call window.

Merge resolutions:
1. One id and fact collision. g06b-kenji-gift-note-status and g09b-kenji-gift-note-status test the same lookup clause, 'gift note text is not recorded on the order' (lookup_order LH-81660). g09b therefore folds into g06b, which keeps the customer frame where every recorded miss occurs (g06 verdict 9) and takes g09b's patterns and fixtures. That leaves g09 with one child, g09a. The pending-gift-note goal at /home/user/agent/tmp/bench/results/g06/REPORT.md:104 is the same test and is not added.
2. One rule is shared on purpose. g03e and g05b test the seed-2 rule from opposite sides: it does not cover Grace's $148.50 replacement, and it does cover Luis's $289.00 refund. Both keep their place, and one corrected FACTS line in the scratch audit.js copy serves both.
3. One parent question is ruled. Each split replaces its parent in the tally. The parent's original request survives only as an unscored bridge position (see scenarioPlan).

Second question, where the harness lives (FINAL-CHECK.md:3, :9-13, :15, :115):
- Records arm: /home/user/agent/tmp/bench3/bench.mjs --mode ledger --profile refined --records on.
- Full view and compaction: /home/user/agent/tmp/bench/bench.mjs.
- Sequencing: /home/user/agent/tmp/bench/results/v7/tools/series.ts, run-one.ts, and plan.ts.
- Live port: /home/user/agent-port/tmp/bench4/driver.mjs.
- Scoring: /home/user/agent/tmp/bench/rescore.mjs, with the audit in /home/user/agent/tmp/bench/results/v10/tools/audit.js and tally.ts.

Third question, a non-Qwen model: the recorded agents are qwen3.5:2b-q4_K_M and qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M (FINAL-CHECK.md:21-22). Picking an equal or better non-Qwen model needs a speed and quality reading that this read-only lane cannot take, because it may send nothing to 127.0.0.1:11434. That choice goes to the Orchestrator. The 6 model-track goals are where a second model family is read.

goals.notes: Lane: objective. Single held, with required changes. 1. R1 was miscounted: 5da23c93 met R1 (a1-pass-1.json:87), and its failure is R5. 2. The proposal's R4 and the fee half of its R6 duplicate R3, so they merge into R3. 3. The audited rows hold 4 non-correct rows, not 3, and t4 is 4 of 4 in each arm. 4. Pattern (b) is narrowed to 243.65, and pattern (c) is widened to every other ticket's ids and totals. Mutation check: if (a) loses `(?:restocking\s+)?`, the a8c30a57 fixture passes. 6. The hedged-then-settled standard (T2) is referred to the Orchestrator, with evidence verdicts-u9.json:8, :63, :99. 7. UNRESOLVED: the proposal's 'Both arms showed the seed-44 withdrawal' cites no recorded prompt. Outside the claims: pattern (a)'s gap also exists in g03 and g05 (b3-pass.json:197, c1-fail.json:199) and is referred to the Orchestrator. Merge: g01 is position 1 in every shift of the rotation, and the band scores it from shift 1. Pattern (c) forbids LH-77302 and 148.50, which g03d expects; the two rule sets apply to different goals, so they do not conflict. Terminal: CHANGES-REQUIRED.

split.request: Grace Okafor still wants a replacement for her missing duvet. Whose sign-off does that replacement need before it ships?
split.tests: R1: who signs off on Grace's replacement.
split.reliesOn: Seed 18, with seed 2 for the full name.
split.scoring: Mechanical: expected ['marcus'], and keep pattern #6 with three amendments. Without #6, the reply 'Tomasz Brennan signs off; Marcus only issues refund codes' passes, and records replies do pull Tomasz into Grace's note (742b972a, 77e6fad6). (1) In alternative 1, widen the separator `(?:\s*[-–—])?\s+` to `(?:\s*[-–—:])?\s+`. (2) Add the alternative `\bmarcus\b(?:\s+oyelaran\b)?\s*\([^()\n]*\b(?:sign|approv)`. (3) In alternative 2, widen `(?:\s+(?:is\s+)?required)?` to `(?:\s+(?:is\s+)?(?:required|authority|needed))?`. Fixtures that pass: 'Sign-off Authority: Marcus Oyelaran', 'Marcus Oyelaran (Escalations Manager): Must sign off on all replacements', 'Marcus Oyelaran (sign-off required)', and '**Sign-off Required:** Marcus'. Fixtures that fail: 'Not Marcus — Tomasz Brennan signs off' and 'Tomasz Brennan signs off; Marcus only issues refund codes'. Caveat: seed 2 names Marcus as escalations manager, and records always shows seed 2 as a rule, so a pass does not prove that seed 18 was delivered.

synthesis.scoringPlan:
Lane: objective. The plan scores the recorded replies per requirement with no further runs. It reports the arm track and the model track apart.

1. Inputs, all read-only. The reply text comes from:
- /home/user/agent/tmp/bench/results/v9/a1-control-v1..v8/none.jsonl.
- /home/user/agent-port/tmp/bench4/results/{p1-ledger,a5-records}-v1..v8/ledger.jsonl.
- /home/user/agent/tmp/bench/results/v10/t4-records-v1..v4/ledger.jsonl and t4-control-v1..v4/none.jsonl.
- The audit item files: /home/user/agent-port/tmp/bench4/audit/{u9,a1}-*.json and /home/user/agent/tmp/bench/results/v10/audit/{b1..b5,c1,d1,d2,e1,e2,e3,r1}-*.json, joined to run and copy through the audit-keys files.

Tool calls are read from each row's firstWire and lastWire fields in the matching -wire directory.

2. Reader. A scratch script imports compileRules and scoreText (/home/user/agent/tmp/bench/rescore.mjs:16, :80) and applies each child goal's rule set to every recorded reply of its parent.
- It never calls main, because main refuses rows whose scenario's scoring fields differ (rescore.mjs:169-177) and reads only scenario.json (:9, :236).
- It never edits rescore.mjs, scenario.json, u2/, or results/v10.

synthesis.risks:
Lane: objective. The risks a split carries, each with its mitigation:

1. Requests that become answerable without context.
- g08b, g08c, and g08d name LH-31055, and g06a, g06b, and g06d name LH-81660, so they no longer test account or order resolution. Only g08a (a ceiling goal that the full view gives away through g04's LH-31055 result, METHOD-DEEP-DIVE.md:270) and g06c keep resolution.
- g05a supplies the over-$200 condition. A context-blind reply still fails it, because MX-4471 (seeds 2 and 3) is the only code it could guess.
- A guessed 'today' would pass g07b on the word alone, so its expectedAny holds date forms only.
- A context-blind 'no code needed' passes g03e only when the audit accepts a reply without the over-$200 scope as the reason. Rule that standard before auditing.
- g04b passes an empty or ticket-free reply. Report the count of replies without 'esc-2219' beside it.
- g02's card is already in the full view's history from g01 (4 of 8 a1 runs).

2. Facts that two goals share.
- Seed 6 holds both the Priya copy rule (g03b, and g04b's lure) and the delivery-date rule (g06a) (scenario.json seed[6]).
- Seed 2 serves g03a's full name, g03e, g05a, and g05b. g03e and g05b judge one rule from opposite sides, and one FACTS line serves both.
- Seed 8 serves g07a and g07b. Seed 11 serves g06c and g09a. Seed 24 serves g10a and g10b, and g03d forbids its 4127.
- PW-5521-9930 is g03c's answer and g06c's decoy.
- Seeds 44 and 45 serve g01 R3 and g05b's withdrawal scope.
- lookup LH-31055 serves all g08 children and g10a's decoy.
- The gift-note lookup clause was tested twice (g06b and g09b) until the merge.

The rotation keeps sharing goals in different shifts where one goal's answer would leak into another's history. That leak reaches the full view only, because records drop earlier goal runs (bench3/bench.mjs:133-134). g09a and g06b share shift 2; report that reading apart, with an 'aiko' diagnostic on the g06b reply.

3. Lost long-distance recall and lost constructs.
- The split drops the compound selection failure, omitting a value in view while answering several things (g06 R3b, records 5 of 16). It is measured only on the recorded rows.
- g04's cross-thread binding (R5) is scored only in g03d.
- g09's carryover lure from the model's own g06 claims (R2, 7 of 29 against 0 of 34) survives only as a side finding in g09a's audit.
- g08's resolution from seed 22 or 36 survives only in a ceiling goal.
- The kept far-recall tests are g01 (seed 4 against 44), g04a (seeds 22 to 28), g05a (seed 29 against 2), g06c and g09a (seed 11), g07a and g07b (seed 8), and g10a and g10b (seed 24).

4. Comparability.
- Shorter child answers shrink the full view's prompt against the recorded series, which can lift the full view. This lift is a real effect of the split, not drift, but it breaks direct comparison with the recorded bands. The bridge positions carry the old requests so the recorded parent rates can be checked against the rotation.
- The per-copy scale changes from 10 goals to 19 arm-track goals. The per-parent weighting keeps each topic at weight 1, and the Orchestrator rules it (FINAL-CHECK.md:48).
- Copy wording confounds g09 R2 and g10 R7 (both cluster on v4).
- The records fit stays in-sample (FINAL-CHECK.md:44).

5. Scoring hazards.
- Four patterns exist only as descriptions or have open holes: g06b's claim pattern, g07b's wrong-date pattern, g08d's standalone-760 guard, and g08c's $760 exemption. Pattern (a)'s gap in g03 and g05 (b3-pass.json:197, c1-fail.json:199) is also open. None of them may score until it passes its fixtures.
- wordMatcher treats a comma as a boundary (rescore.mjs:69-71).
- Five audit standards are inconsistent in the recorded verdicts (see scoringPlan item 4).
- The thinking cap's empty replies (FINAL-CHECK.md:31-33) are a harness effect and must not count as a context failure.

- Keeping the ceiling goals g07c and g08a.

- The Marcus-origin replay (g07).

goals.notes:
Lane: objective (correctness and what the contracts permit).

Design: g03 asks for 3 things (R1 to R3), and every arm and model meets them (24 of 24, 23 of 24, and 24 of 24 at 2B thinking off; 8 of 8 at 4B with thinking). The outcome is decided by things the request never asks for: the full view binds another thread's ticket (R4, 8 of 8 a1-control), and records adds wrong people or misapplies the approval code (R4, R5, R7). The existing g03 therefore measures binding by accident. g03d makes binding the scored goal. g03a to g03c keep the asked facts as clean context goals. g03e isolates the rule-scope error, the only failure left at 4B with thinking.

Alternative: keep g03 whole and only add \besc-\d{4}\b to its forbidden patterns. Rejected because R5 and R7 would still decide records outcomes and the goal would still score three things.

Refusals: no goal for R7. The scenario must not score what 'no seed or lookup' decides, and nothing states who must not be copied. No restocking patterns on any split goal, because they test nothing in Grace's case (R8).

Constraints: scenario.json:1 (seed 2, 6, 13 to 19, 22 to 28; g03 fields); u2/rules.json:13-23; audit.js:36, :48, :64; rescore.mjs:61, :170-177; bench.mjs:2297; FINAL-CHECK.md:94, :142.

Measurements read: verdicts-u9 and verdicts-a1 (2B thinking off, 8 copies per arm), verdicts-e1 to e3 (t4, 4 copies), and three c1 items. Missing: the f4 copies 1 to 8 g03 verdicts (keys d1 and d2) and the r1 items, which I did not read.

Units: (U1, executor) write g03a to g03e and their 8 rewordings into scenario.json, variants/v1-8.json, and variants/ledger/v1-8.json with identical scoring fields (rescore.mjs:170-177 refuses a mismatch). Acceptance: every expected string sits in its listed seed or lookup and in none of the requests. (U2, executor) add fixtures for each g03d pattern and the g03c guard: pass cases include 'Copy: Priya Raman' and 'Tracking PW-5521-9930'; fail cases include 'Ticket: ESC-2291 (now ESC-2219)' and 'Escalating Ticket: LH-77302'. Acceptance: all fixtures pass. (U3, executor) the per-requirement rescoring script over the existing item files, writing to scratch, never editing results. (U4, checker on Haiku) a one-requirement audit for g03e and R5 over the existing replies, with FACTS fixed for seed 19.

Tensions: (1) Adding 5 requests lengthens the shift and moves every later goal's distance (FINAL-CHECK.md:142). The Orchestrator rules on order, or runs the split goals as their own shift. (2) g03d's expectedAny partly overlaps g03c; the alternative is the bare request alone, which an off-topic reply could pass. (3) g03e's track: both arms deliver seeds 2, 15, and 29, so it is model track, but whether records places the code rule beside Marcus is unmeasured. (4) g03a can be answered from seed 2 alone.

Risks: the auditor FACTS omits seed 19, which produced 3 false 'unsupported trace' readings. Auditors also misdiagnosed pattern #6's markdown handling in 3 items.

Lane: objective.

Design: g04's scored requirement (R1 and R2) never decides an outcome: 0 real misses in 32 audited replies. The outcome is decided by an element that cannot be met ('Send her the number', when send_reply only reaches the shift lead), by false claims of having sent or copied (7 of 16 records replies at 2B thinking off), and by stray values (2 of 8 in the full view). The split removes the unmeetable ask from g04a, so g04a scores the correction alone. g04b keeps the original wording and scores only whether the reply claims an action it cannot perform.

Alternative: drop R3 and R4 entirely and keep only g04a. That is simpler, but it discards the one reading on g04 that differs by arm at 2B thinking off. R5 gets no g04 goal of its own, because g03d already measures binding; give a construct one home.

Refusals: no goal that scores 'the number reached Priya', because no tool can deliver it (bench.mjs:2297).

Constraints: scenario.json:1 (seeds 22, 23, 27, 28; g04 tools ['send_reply']); u2/rules.json:66-69; bench.mjs:2297; rescore.mjs:116, :122, :170-177; FINAL-CHECK.md:115; u2/compare.md:15.

Measurements read: verdicts-u9, verdicts-a1, and verdicts-e1 to e3 for every g04 item. Missing: the f4 copies 1 to 8 and t2a g04 verdicts (keys d1, d2, c1), which I did not read.

(U2, executor) fixtures for the amended g04a pattern and the g04b patterns. (U3) is shared with g03: score the existing items per requirement.

In one shift, the later request inherits the earlier answer, so run them in separate shifts or far apart.

3. R3: count HELD, evidence FAILED. 'LH-77302 appears only in seed 13' is false: it also appears in seed 14 (the call_1 arguments), seed 15, and seed 17 (scenario.json:1).
4. R4: the full-view count HELD (8 of 8, verdicts-a1.json:147-152, :434-494). The records count FAILED: it is 4 of 16, not 3, because 77e6fad6 copies 'Tomasz Brennan (Warehouse - for release coordination)' (verdicts-u9.json:354). Two citations FAILED. FINAL-CHECK.md:93-94 describes the 4B with thinking off, not t4. Card 7719 is not in seeds 40 to 45; it is in lookup_customer LH-44870 (scenario.json:1 tools).
5. R5: armSensitive FAILED. At 4B the full view has 3 of 4 (01a79561, verdicts-e1.json:80; 191b9e52, verdicts-e2.json:45; e2a9fc37, verdicts-e1.json:108) against records 0 of 4. The proposal also missed t2a 35b6ea7f (verdicts-c1.json:80). Tension (3)'s claim that this is 'unmeasured' is false. The requirement is renamed, because no seed forbids writing the code; it only scopes the code to refunds over $200.
6. R6: count HELD. Attack: 'No code is needed; MX-4471 doesn't apply' hits #8 (u2/rules.json:22) while it meets R5, so the claim that R6 'arises only when R5 is already broken' holds for the recorded replies and not for g03e's request.
7. R7: counts HELD. Kind FAILED: the word 'internal' in the request decides it, not form and not a seed, so the kind is reasoning.
8. R8: HELD (u2/rules.json:15-19; no hit in any g03 verdict read).
9. R9: FAILED. Four reply-side invented claims exist (verdicts-a1.json:439, :457; verdicts-c1.json:225; verdicts-u9.json:363). Only the 'trace not opened' flags are auditor errors.
10. R10: HELD (bench.mjs:2297).
11. g03a: FAILED. Dropping #6 lets 'Tomasz Brennan signs off; Marcus only issues refund codes' pass on 'marcus'. The fix is to keep #6 with the three amendments in g03a's scoring field.

The u2 rules for g06 already map one pattern to one requirement: the forbidden list with patterns 1 and 2 to R1, pattern 3 to R7, pattern 4 to R5, pattern 5 to R2 (incomplete), and the expected tracking number to R3b. rescore.mjs:102-108 already names each hit by pattern index, so a driver that imports compileRules and scoreText can tally misses per requirement, run, and arm over p1-ledger-v1..v8 and a5-records-v1..v8 (/home/user/agent-port/tmp/bench4/results/*/ledger.jsonl), plus a1-control and the v10 rows once located. goals.notes:
Lane: objective.

Design: split g06 into four single-requirement goals. g06a (R1, arm) and g06c (R3a and R3b, arm) test what the context delivers. g06b (R2, model) and g06d (R6, model) test what the lookup and the system date give every arm equally. g06a, g06b, and g06d name LH-81660, so only g06c depends on seed 11.

Alternatives: REPORT.md:104 proposes a two-way split into withhold-the-estimate and pending-gift-note goals. Rejected because its withhold goal still carries the tracking requirement (R3b missed in 5 of 16 records replies), the addressee requirement (11 of 16), and the 'today' slip (20 of 48 plain-rule replies, REPORT.md:74), so it would stay compound.

Constraints: REPORT.md:102-104 says the rule reaches every prompt in both arms and directs a reword of seed 6. rules.json:36-43 holds g06's five patterns. The rendered forms of dates must be declared in /home/user/agent/tmp/bench/dated/table.json, and dated/check.mjs must exit 0 (REPORT.md:7-9). rescore.mjs:9 reads only scenario.json, so split scoring needs its own driver.

Refusals: a standalone R5 addressee goal and a standalone R7 delivered-claim goal. The R5 goal is foreclosed by the brief's rule 'Keep each split request answerable only from the context or the lookup, never from the request alone', because a context-blind 'Hi Kenji' passes pattern 4. R7 decides no audited outcome in the evidence read.

Measurements: supplied: verdicts-u9 (16 g06 items), verdicts-a1 (8), and verdicts-e1..e3 (8), plus REPORT.md's 4-condition series, replays, and probes. Missing: f4 and t2a g06 verdicts from v10; the location of the a1-control and v10 row files; and tool-call logs showing whether the 5 records replies that miss the tracking number called lookup_order.

Units: U1 adds g06a to g06d to /home/user/agent/tmp/bench/split/goals.json, with 8 rewordings each, and the new date strings to dated/table.json. Executor on Claude Sonnet. Acceptance: expected strings appear in a listed fact or lookup and in no request; dated/check.mjs exits 0. U2 fixtures for the new g06a, g06b, and g06d patterns from the quoted replies. Executor on Claude Haiku. Acceptance: scoreText agrees with every label. Depends on U1. U3 per-requirement rescore of the recorded g06 rows (the same split/requirements.mjs as g05). Acceptance: reproduces rescore.mjs on the original rules. U4 per-requirement audit for R2, R3a (from the tool calls), and R6. Executor on Claude Sonnet, with Claude Haiku checkers. Acceptance: 0 unresolved.

Tensions: (a) g06a is on the arm track by classification (seed 6 is a far rule), but the evidence shows the arms failing alike (FINAL-CHECK.md:130). The Orchestrator rules whether g06a runs on the recorded wording or the plain wording that REPORT.md:103 recommends; under 'never promise' it reads the wording defect, not the arm. (b) The addressee miss R5 differs by arm (11 of 16 records against 3 of 8 full view), and the refusal leaves it unscored. (c) g06b asks the shift lead, not the customer; whether the customer-facing lure is what the owner wants measured is a judgment call. (d) Four goals replace one, which weights Kenji's ticket four times in a per-copy pass count.

Risks: g06d's expected values move with the run-day frame. The invented-window pattern can hit 'by Friday' in an unrelated sentence. g06c and g09 both rely on seed 11, so a records drop of seed 11 costs two goals.

Lane: objective (correctness against the verdict files, the scorer contract, and the arm mechanics).

Verdicts on the proposal:
1. R1 count: HELD. Records miss 4 of 16, a1 misses 7 of 8, and the 4B misses 0 of 8 (key-u9-fail.json:39-198, key-a1-fail.json:45-192, verdicts-e1/e2/e3). CORRECTED: 2 of the 4 records misses have no note at all (R7), and 5 of the 7 a1 misses are independent of R3.
2. R1 and R2 as separate requirements: FAILED. They test one correction, seed 29. They are merged, and g05a already scores them together.
3. R3a and R3b split: FAILED. No reply separates them, and 33a0d960 is a third mode, withdrawal-scope overreach, not a comparison misread. 'Seed 44 cannot change the result' is false. R3b armSensitive false contradicts its own counts (3 of 8 against 0 of 16).
4. R7 count and arm call: FAILED. Records miss it in 6 of 20, not 4, and 7e0c5b90 and 9cbd7777 were omitted. It differs by arm against 0 of 12, so it is armSensitive true.
5. R6 count: FAILED. u9 misses it in 2 of 16, not 1 (a2b148b4).
6. g05a 'no audit needed': FAILED. It conflicts with tally.ts's adjudication (FINAL-CHECK.md:48).
7. g05b request: FAILED. 'which of our refund rules apply ... what each one needs' asks two things. It solicits the restocking rule (R4, decided by seed 44) and the code (R1), and the audit judges both while the scorer scores neither. expected ['approval'] passes a context-blind generic answer. Pattern (1) fails correct restatements through its 'without' branch, and pattern (4) fails 'not under $200'. The corrected request and scoring are in split.
8. 'Rows not located': FAILED. The paths are in scoreExisting.

Findings outside the claims: d120b387's audit refers the question of whether the Priya copy rule (seed 6) applies to a refund authorization (verdicts-e1.json:181). The seed calls only escalations, so no requirement follows. Referred to the Orchestrator only if the owner reads a refund authorization as an escalation.

Attacked and held: R5's counts and ids. Refusing g05c and a standalone R7 goal: a context-blind reply passes either check, by the brief's rule as quoted. Dropping R4 to g01, given the corrected g05b request. Tensions (b) and (c). The rescore.mjs citations (:9, :16, :55-65, :80-91, :102-109, :169-177, :236). The harness pointer (FINAL-CHECK.md:11-13 and :115).

Referred: whether g05a and g05b replace g05 or join it in the per-copy scale (FINAL-CHECK.md:48) goes to the Orchestrator.

goals.notes:
Lane: objective (correctness and what the scorer and audit contracts permit).

Design: split g07 into g07a (who, arm track), g07b (deadline date frame, model track, scored only where seed 8 reached the prompt), and g07c (pro number, arm track). R5 and R6 stay audit points, not goals: they apply to every reply, and no token can score them. Each arm loses g07 on a different requirement, as in g06 (results/g06/REPORT.md:104). The 2B full view loses R1 (Marcus, 4 of 8). The 2B records arm loses R3 (Friday-today, 5 of 16). The 4B with thinking loses neither (8 of 8 correct). The g07 records lead in the a1 comparison therefore mixes an arm effect (R1) with a model effect (R3).

Alternatives: (1) Keep R1 and R2 together as one seed-8 goal. One message supports both, but R2 is met by replies that miss seed 8 ('Reach out to Marcus today', 90fa887a), so a combined goal would not score one thing; rejected. (2) Run each split goal alone from the seed, as the g06-only series did (REPORT.md:16). Isolation favors this, but it removes the earlier answers that cause the full view's Marcus error (INVESTIGATE-4B.md:254). That error is part of what the strategy shows, so I rejected this in favor of rotation sets (see Units).

Constraints: scenario.json:1 (g07 expected, expectedAny, forbiddenPatterns, facts [8,36], tools); rescore.mjs:84-85 (an expectedAny phrase matches only between non-letters and non-digits); rescore.mjs:169-177 (rows naming another scenario with different fields are refused); audit.js:36 (FACTS for g07); audit.js:47-48 and :65 (pass and fail standards); FINAL-CHECK.md:48 (tally rules); FINAL-CHECK.md:94 (the 4B removes the who-is-who errors on g07).

Refusals: a split request that names Tomasz or 'today' would leak the answer, which the brief forbids ('does not leak its answer'). No new run comes from this lane ('Never send any request to 127.0.0.1:11434').

Measurements supplied (keys key-u9-*.json, key-a1-*.json, key-e*-*.json; verdict files as cited). 2B thinking off: records 6 correct, 3 ambiguous, 7 wrong of 16; full view 3 correct, 5 wrong of 8. t4: 8 of 8 correct in both arms. Missing: how often a model guesses 'today' without seed 8; per-requirement rates under single-question requests; per-item f4 verdicts (only INVESTIGATE-4B.md:89-91 cited, b-series verdicts not read).

Units. U1, implementer, cheap engine (Sonnet): writes tmp/bench/split/rules.json (g07a, g07b, g07c, g08a, g08b, g08c rule sets) and tmp/bench/split/score-split.mjs, which imports compileRules and scoreText, reads recorded rows read-only, writes per-requirement tables, and applies g07b's seed-8 condition. Acceptance: on the u9 and a1 rows it reproduces R1 records 1 of 16 against full view 4 of 8, and R3 records 5 of 16 against full view 1 of 8; every new pattern has fixtures in the shape of u2/fixtures.json, and all pass. No dependency. U2, checker on Haiku through an audit.js-shaped workflow with one point per item: re-audits 9123d3ae, 2bedbe9b, e1077cc9, and 089494cc on R1 alone. Acceptance: 0 unresolved. Depends on U1's split. U3, author on Sonnet: writes the split goals into a scenario copy plus variants v1 to v8 and ledger v1 to v8, reworded and fact-preserving. Acceptance: each expected token appears in its named seed message or lookup and in no request, as the scenario notes check. Depends on U1's rules. U4 (Orchestrator, new runs): rotation run sets, each asking one child per parent family, so no sibling answer sits in view before its sibling. Depends on U3.

Tensions: (a) R3 skews toward records on the 2B with thinking off (5 of 16 against 1 of 8), yet it shows up in the full view under 2B thinking (INVESTIGATE-4B.md:92). I ruled it model track; the Orchestrator rules whether the records rendering of seed 8 as a standing rule counts as part of the strategy. (b) R5 is audit-only and is not a goal. (c) The rotation design is cross-goal and needs the other analysts' families.

Risks: g07b's seed-8 condition shrinks n for records whenever seed 8 drops out. The full view carries sibling answers in any single-sequence run (a g07a reply usually says 'today'), so without rotation g07b leaks in the full view only.

goals.notes:
Lane: objective.

Design: split g08 into g08a (account resolution and manager, arm track), g08b (fit verdict, model track, id given in the request), and g08c (available credit, model track, id given in the request). The arms fail g08 on different requirements. On the 2B with thinking off, records lose R3 (11 of 16) and the full view loses R4 (3 of 8), so g08's records-against-full-view result (records 4 correct of 16; full view 5 correct, 3 wrong of 8) compares two different skills. R1 and R2 never fail. That makes g08a a near-ceiling goal: it keeps the one arm-sensitive step and adds little separation.

Alternatives: (1) Score the remaining credit after the reorder ($760) in g08c. The $2,000 errors favor it (d18abfe6, e9372aad), but it chains two subtractions and implies a verdict, so it is not one thing; rejected. (2) Leave the id out of g08b and g08c. That keeps them arm-sensitive through R1, which never fails, and mixes context into a model goal; rejected. (3) Drop g08a as a ceiling goal; this is the Orchestrator's call (Tension b).

Constraints: scenario.json:1 (g08 fields and notes trap (b): g08's lookup puts 555-0142 in view as g10's decoy); u2/rules.json:51-64 (corrected g08 patterns); rescore.mjs:84-85 and :169-177; audit.js:36 and :48; METHOD-DEEP-DIVE.md:232-246 (losses by stage); FINAL-CHECK.md:110 (t4 records hold 2 to 3 of 4 on g08 because the verdict is missing).

Refusals: a g08b request that says 'it fits' or gives $3,760 would leak the answer and is foreclosed by the brief. Running the split live is outside this lane (no request to 127.0.0.1:11434).

Measurements supplied: per-id verdicts as cited (verdicts-u9.json, verdicts-a1.json, verdicts-e1.json to e3.json, with their keys). Missing: g08b under a single-question request; the 2B records verdict rate with earlier explicit answers present (the priming inference is unmeasured, METHOD-DEEP-DIVE.md:272).

Units: shared with g07 (U1 rule sets and reader, U2 one-point re-audit of d18abfe6, e9372aad, and f61f0cec, U3 split scenario and variants, U4 rotation run sets). g08-specific acceptance for U1: on the u9 and a1 rows it reproduces R3 records 11 of 16 against full view 0 of 8, and R4 records 3 of 16 against full view 3 of 8.

Tensions: (a) R3 is the same input in every arm, but the 2B full view, which carries its own earlier explicit answers, never drops the verdict, while records drop it in 11 of 16. I ruled R3 model track because no seed fact decides it. The Orchestrator rules whether answer-shape priming from earlier answers counts as a context-strategy effect; if it does, g08b moves to the arm track without the id in the request. (b) Keep or drop g08a, given 0 failures in 32 replies. (c) The 'plenty of room' additions to expectedAny need fixtures.

Risks: g10's 555-0142 decoy depends on a lookup_customer LH-31055 call before g10 (scenario.json:1 notes trap (b)). Every rotation set has to keep one g08 child ahead of g10, and the three children add repeated lookups to the full view, which changes its prompt length. In the full view the LH-31055 result can already be in view from an earlier goal (METHOD-DEEP-DIVE.md:270), which gives g08a away in that arm.

Lane: objective (correctness under the scorer and audit contracts, count truth, letter of the rules).

Verdicts
1. Counts: HELD after re-derivation from key-u9-pass/fail.json, key-a1-pass/fail.json, key-e1..e3, and the verdict files. Records: 6 correct, 3 ambiguous, 7 wrong of 16. Full view: 3 correct, 5 wrong of 8. t4: 8 of 8 correct. Exception: the 4B thinking-off claim of 4 of 4 covers copies 1 to 4 of 8; copies 5 to 8 are NOT-EVIDENCED.
2. 'INVESTIGATE-4B.md:254 traces the Marcus error to earlier full-view answers': UNRESOLVED. Line 254 asserts that errors spread and cites only the g03-to-g05 template (INVESTIGATE-4B.md:116). The rejection of Alternative (2) rests on this claim. Refer to the Orchestrator: a single-change replay of the a1 g07 calls with earlier assistant answers removed (the method in results/g06/REPORT.md:31) decides it.
3. R2 and R3 as separate requirements: FAILS. They are one scored requirement (evidence in R2). The proposal's g07b 'tests R3' also tests the deadline itself.
4. R3 armSensitive false, g07b model track: FAILS. Same model and settings, different rendering: p1 fails 4 of 8, a5 fails 1 of 8 (FINAL-CHECK.md:115,125). The records failures take one fused form, and the full-view failures take others. 'Shows up in both arms' does not make the inputs equal. g07b moves to the arm track and its seed-8 gating goes. The Orchestrator can add a model-track control.
5. R5 failure count: understated (3 unjudged records replies with the identical wording); armSensitive set to true.
6. g07a optional patterns: FAIL (false failures on correct replies); dropped.
7. g07b scoring: FAILS. 'today' alone passes a request for the day and date; no pattern catches 'today (Thursday 2026-10-09)'; its date-bound tokens sit outside the dated pipeline (dated/check.mjs:6,55-58).
8. g07c request changes a fact (the blocker): reworded.
9. U1 acceptance 'R3 records 5 of 16': fails under its own rule (6 of 16).
10. U2 target point: wrong (R1); corrected to R4 and R5.

Findings outside the claims
- The proposal's U3 acceptance says each expected token appears in a seed message or lookup and in no request. That holds for g07, but for a computed g08 value it cannot hold (see the g08 notes).

- Every reworded copy carries the seed-8 sentence verbatim: held (variants/v1..v8.json and variants/ledger/v1..v8.json).

- The rescore.mjs main refusal: held (rescore.mjs:169-177).

goals.notes:
Lane: objective.

Verdicts
1. Counts: HELD after re-derivation. Records: 4 correct, 12 real of 16. R3 11 of 16. Figure errors 3 of 16 (1 now, 2 post-reorder). Full view: 5 correct, 3 wrong of 8. t4 records: 2 correct, 1 real, 1 ambiguous; t4 full view: 4 of 4 correct (verdicts-e1..e3.json with key-e*.json).
2. R3 armSensitive false and 'inputs are identical across arms': FAILS. The lookup result is identical, but the prompt is not (METHOD-DEEP-DIVE.md:265-270). On the 2B with thinking off, all 11 omissions sit in the 16 records replies and none in the 8 full-view replies; t2a and t4 point the same way. g08b moves to the arm track. The Orchestrator still rules whether answer-shape priming counts as a context-strategy effect (the proposal's Tension a). If it does not, a model-track read of R3 needs a single-change replay, because no request wording equalizes the two arms' prompts.
3. R3 kind reasoning: FAILS; the kind is form (no reply states a wrong direction).
4. R4 as one requirement: FAILS. Available-now and post-reorder errors are disjoint sets, and the post-reorder set is 5 of the 7 2B figure errors. The proposed g08c never asks for a post-reorder figure, and g08b drops #11, so the split loses coverage the original goal had. Added g08d.
5. g08b 'room for': FAILS (a false-pass path); dropped.
6. g08c with #10 unchanged: FAILS on a correct '$760 available after the reorder' aside.
7. U1 R4 acceptance: not mechanically reproducible (see scoreExisting).
8. U3 acceptance ('each expected token appears in its named seed message or lookup'): cannot hold for computed values (3,760 and 760 appear in no seed or lookup). Exempt derived values by name.
9. Rotation and the g10 decoy: HELD as a risk. Also, g04 already puts LH-31055 and 555-0142 in the full view (METHOD-DEEP-DIVE.md:270), so the g10 decoy does not depend on a g08 child.

Findings outside the claims
- The live g08 rule u2 #10 (u2/rules.json:62) fails a correct reply that adds '$760 available after the reorder'. No audited reply says it, so no recorded verdict changes, but the corrected rules carry the hole.
- The audit is inconsistent on figures-only replies: 8608607c was ruled real after a tie (verdicts-u9.json:1413-1419) and f61f0cec ambiguous (verdicts-e2.json:176-182) on the same shape. Refer to the Orchestrator to rule once, before g08b is scored.

Attacked and held
- R1 and R2 have 0 failures: held. Albrecht exists only in the canned lookup (scenario.json:1 tools).
- The id in the g08b, g08c, and g08d requests leaks no answer: held (no figure or verdict in any request).
- g08 patterns #1 to #9 are u2/rules.json:53-61, #10 is :62, #11 is :63: held.

Terminal: g08 is compound and splits into 4 goals: g08a (arm), g08b (arm), g08c (model), and g08d (model). 8 required changes follow from verdicts 2 to 8, and 2 referrals go to the Orchestrator (priming as strategy; the figures-only audit standard).

(2) The audit brief judges the whole reply (audit.js:64-65), so a split goal still fails on an unrelated weekday slip. Single-requirement scoring needs a brief that rules only the goal's requirement and logs the rest as side findings. That is a method change for the Orchestrator. (3) Dropping pattern #1 moves weekday errors out of scoring entirely. If the owner wants them measured, they belong in one model-track date goal, not in g10. A g10a reply often already states 'after 2 pm' (u9 3b2e7551), which turns a later g10b into a near recall, so separate the siblings by sequence or by run.
